     Ohio Buckeye. Sapindaceæ.

     A beautiful tree growing in the bottom lands of the Ohio river. The tincture is to be made of the whole fruit ; the bark may differ. Symptoms mostly toxic ; provings commenced only by Hale.

   

MIND. [1] [Æsc. g.]
Confusion of mind, with vertigo, often followed by stupefaction and coma.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Æsc. g.]
Vertigo with staggering, reeling, unconsciousness.
Vertigo with full, heavy head, dim sight, thick speech, nausea and vomiting.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Æsc. g.]
Fulness and heaviness in head without pain, with vertigo and faintness towards evening.
(OBS :) According to the wry neck, the vertigo, sensation of fulness and heaviness of head, stupor, great weakness and trembling of limbs, it may be used in meningitis.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Æsc. g.]
Sight dim or lost.
Eyes fixed and dead.
Eyes expressionless.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Æsc. g.]
Speech thick and tongue as if lame.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Æsc. g.]
Nausea, with loathing of food and vomiting.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Æsc. g.]
Cramplike pain.
Sensation of fulness.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Æsc. g.]
Distension (with cattle).
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Æsc. g.]
Hard, knotty stools.
Constipation.
Very painful, dark purple hemorrhoidal tumors, with lame back and lower limbs.
It is popular to carry the fruit in the breeches-pocket, as a preventive of piles.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Æsc. g.]
Wry neck (cattle).
Great lameness and weakness of back.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Æsc. g.]
Trembling of lower limbs.
Hind limbs lame ; falling (cattle).
A strong tendency to contraction of legs.
   

NERVES. [36] [Æsc. g.]
Spasms and convulsions, followed by lameness (cattle).
Great weakness.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Æsc. g.]
Stupor and confusion, followed by coma.
   

TIME. [38] [Æsc. g.]
Towards evening : vertigo and faintness.
   

FEVER. [40] [Æsc. g.]
Some typhoid symptoms.
   

SENSATIONS. [43] [Æsc. g.]
Pain : in hemorrhoids.
Cramplike pain : in stomach.
Fulness and heaviness : in head ; in stomach.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Æsc. g.]
Collateral relations : Æsc. hipp.
Discrete relations : Aloes ; Colinsonia ; Ignat. ; Nux vom.
